note: _nisi conversi fueritis ut efficiamini sicut parvulis_ – unless you become like children again. On constructions with _convertere_ (to turn) to say “again,” see the glossary s.v. _convertere, conversus_ (Chapter 19.2). – Edmund F. Sutcliffe SJ: “Et tu aliquando conversus,” St Luke 22,32. _Catholic Biblical Quarterly_ 15 (1953) 305–310, at pp. 308–309.

_redde quod debes –_ pay what thou owest (Douay Version). This is a formulaic request, known from Petronius (_Saturae_ 57,5 – cena Trimalchionis), no doubt belonging to the language of law and business. – Friedrich Stummer: “Via peccantium complanata lapidibus” (Eccli 21,11), in: Bonifatius Fischer – Virgil Fiala (eds.): _Colligere fragmenta. Festsschrift Alban Dold_. Beuron 1952 (xx, 295 pp.), pp. 42–44, at p. 42. ▲
